info.title: API.SH: Medium
info.description: The Medium API from API.SH: public Medium data as clean JSON. Every endpoint is a GET with query parameters and your key in the x-api-key header. Calls that run cost the credits shown (x-credits): successes, and lookups that found nothing (404). Refused calls and errors on our side are free. Docs: https://api.sh/docs · Every platform: https://api.sh/openapi.json

get.description:
A Medium story: title, subtitle, author, publication, tags, claps, responses, reading time, dates, canonical URL (`canonical_url`, the original address for stories first published elsewhere) and the full text (plain text and paragraphs with links and images). Member-only stories return the part Medium shows publicly (`truncated`).

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/medium-post

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
The responses (comments) to a Medium post, 25 per page: id, link, full text, published and updated times, claps, reply count, member-only flag and the author (name, username, link, image, followers), with the total. Pass a response id as `url` to list its replies. Pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor`; null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/medium-post-comments

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Medium post link or post id (a response id lists that response's replies).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
A Medium tag (story and follower counts) and its stories, 10 per page: by default the tag page's recommended feed; `feed` picks the latest stories or the top stories of the week, month, year or all time. Each story has its claps, responses, reading time, tags, dates, member-only flag and `canonical_url`. Pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor` (null on the last page).

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/medium-tag

parameters.name: feed
parameters.description: hot (default, recommended), latest, top_week, top_month, top_year or top_all_time. Keep the same feed when passing `cursor`.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Value of `next_cursor` from the previous page.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Create keys at https://app.api.sh/keys. Authorization: Bearer <key> also works.

raw.name: raw
raw.description: 0 leaves out the bulky `raw` source blocks (often 10-30x smaller).

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. `posts.id,posts.title`. Call metadata is always included.

fresh.name: fresh
fresh.description: 1 skips the 24-hour cache and fetches live.

output.name: output
output.description: csv or ndjson returns the response's records (its main list, or the object as one row) as CSV or NDJSON instead of JSON.

records.name: records
records.description: With output=csv|ndjson: the top-level list to turn into rows (e.g. `reviews`), or `.` for the whole object as one row.

status_url.description: On a 503 for a paused endpoint: the status page, which lists open incidents.

E400.description: A parameter is missing or invalid. Not charged (unless the call ran and the source rejected the value; credits_used says).

E401.description: Missing, invalid, revoked or expired API key. Not charged. See https://api.sh/docs/errors#401

E402.description: Not enough credits, a spend limit you set was reached (`spend_limit`), or the key's monthly credit cap was reached (`key_cap`). Not charged.

E404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

E502.description: The source site failed this time; retry. Not charged.

E503.description: Endpoint paused or temporarily unavailable; may include retry-after, and status_url (https://api.sh/status) for a paused endpoint. Not charged.
